newsitem.title: UK: Exco outlook gloomy, expects final div cut.
newsitem.headline: Exco outlook gloomy, expects final div cut.

text.p: Money and bonds broker Exco Plc, which halved its interim dividend on Tuesday, said there was little evidence to suggest an improvement in volumes and revenues in the remaining months of the year.
As a result, Exco said it was "probable" that it would also recommend a halving of the final dividend.
The company also warned on second half profits.

"Whilst our efforts are concentrated...to ensure that we maintain a sound platform on which to grow in the future, current revenue levels make us cautious about the prospects for the year as a whole," chairman David Hubbard said.
Exco noted that at the time of its last annual results, the chairman said market sentiment appeared to have improved in the early months of 1996 and the year had started more satisfactorily.
"Since March, however, volumes have fallen and brokerage commission rates have again come under renewed pressure as our customers address their own operating costs.
"In common with the rest of the industry, this has inevitably put Exco's revenue levels under further pressure," the company said on Tuesday.
Pre-tax profits in the first half fell to 12.1 million stg from 16.1 million despite a rise in turnover to 113.7 million from 109.8 million.
The company halved its interim dividend to 1.5 pence. Last year, it paid a final dividend of six pence.
Exco shares were down 13 pence, or just under 15 percent, at 74 pence in early trading.
